title: Apron Chat Protocol
excerpt: Apron is a minimal protocol for self-hosted chats. Simple enough to write a server in ~100 lines, powerful enough for rooms, threads, bots, reactions, and more.
content_html:
Apron is a minimal protocol for self-hosted chats. Simple enough to write a server in ~100 lines, powerful enough for rooms, threads, bots, reactions, and more.

For agents: apron.chat/llms.txt links the spec in Markdown, the servers, clients, JSON Schema and wire fixtures to test against.

1.The Protocol

JSON over any transport, like WebSocket. Tiny core and optional incremental capabilities with graceful fallbacks. Build only what you need.

{"method": "server", "params": {"apron": 10, "auth": ["guest"]}}
{"method": "auth", "id": "c1", "params": {"scheme": "guest", "name": "Ada"}}
{"id": "c1", "result": {"you": {"user_id": "guest_1234", "name": "Ada"}}}
{"method": "message", "id": "c2", "params": {"body": {"text": "Hello"}}}
{"method": "message", "params": {"room_id": "general", "from": {"user_id": "guest_1234"}, ...}}
{"id": "c2", "result": {"message_id": "1724803200042"}}

2.Live Demo

Come say "hi" on our public demo server, or point the Apron Web client at your own server.

3.Servers

Reference implementations to run or modify for your use cases.

4.Clients

Join any server with your favourite client, or build your own.

5.FAQ

  • Who are you?
  • Why did you make the Apron Chat Protocol?
  • Is there encryption? Is it safe?
  • Why not XMPP/Matrix/IRCv3/etc?
  • Why not Slack/Discord/Zulip/etc?
  • Why another standard? XKCD 927!
  • How was AI used to create Apron? Is it slop?
  • Is Apron a business?
  • Why is it named Apron?
  • Ok fine, how can I try it?
